protocols.title: Cross-boundary relational structure
protocols.finding: Semantic/source/runtime/machine/cost boundaries are distinct but causally connected. NEI 0.1 implementation defect was exposed at the identity-authority boundary; q-DAG/task boundary remains a distribution seam.

protocols.title: Constraint-structure discovery
protocols.finding: First-win stopping, exact-q equality, sealed-capacity rules, proof/q separation and operation-word identity guards are load-bearing constraints. First-win excludes nonterminal-q authority after terminal transition.

protocols.title: Interface / port correspondence
protocols.finding: Generic IsoMaxTransitionCache and ordinary-WDL solver use the same key interface but have different value-domain ownership. Global Int8 conversion is invalid; consumer-specific WDL specialization is the lawful candidate.

protocols.title: Dependency-topology discovery
protocols.finding: Semantic value dependency is a ranked q DAG while worker execution materializes private subtree occurrences. Existing #89-#95 remain valid candidate refinements; no scheduler winner is promoted.

protocols.title: QU / open-region topology
protocols.finding: Three open regions remain valid: V8 lowering, dynamic hardware cost, and parallel-distribution economics. They are connected constrained unknowns, not missing scalars. No justified QUI between them.

protocols.title: Repeated relational motifs
protocols.finding: Repeated over-general representation motif spans signed hash/isolated-bit, fixed masks, singleton projection, move-order incidence, and remaining hash-mix chain. Repeated same-word move-order loads form a new local motif.

protocols.title: Alternative-factorization discovery
protocols.finding: Residual-first mirror canonicalization can be refactored to support-first without changing the reflection orbit; dense ownTransition can fuse class loading with its existing dense transform.

protocols.title: Residual-structure discovery after partial match
protocols.finding: The initial #73 NEI layer's residual was not a natural distinction but a qualification defect. Corrected 0.2 preserves representation equivalence separately from NEI authority. Lower-confidence residuals: derived support masks and blocker affected-slot traversal.

protocols.title: Symmetry / automorphism discovery
protocols.finding: Horizontal reflection is exact. Support-first orientation can decide asymmetric mirror orbits before residual reflection; residual comparison remains only for support stabilizers. Per-class reflection-order memo is demoted to a symmetric-support fallback.

protocols.title: Role-equivalent elements under different labels
protocols.finding: Signed and unsigned representation occurrences can play the same operation-word role only under the explicit P-ISOMAX-OPERATION-WORD32-0.2 identity law; role match alone is not NEI SAME.

protocols.title: Invariants across admissible variation
protocols.finding: NEI-HOT-001 and -002 are determinate only because exact operation-word projection plus fixed evidence settles identity. #96 remains unqualified because full-chain consumer closure is not yet proved.

protocols.title: Known/unknown interface correspondence
protocols.finding: Known source/runtime observations attach to QU-HOT-01/02/03 at exact boundaries. Hardware counters remain unknown; failure to configure xperf is not zero cost.

protocols.title: Multi-scale common substructure
protocols.finding: The same mismatch pattern appears from bit-level carriers through residual kernels to task scheduling: implementation generality/materialization can exceed semantic need. No claim of one universal mechanism is made.

protocols.title: Transformation-invariant discovery
protocols.finding: Exact results survive signed/unsigned carrier changes, table precomputation, flattening, reflection and preparation reorder. Support-first mirror selection is a new transformation-invariant candidate; hash-mix signing remains pending.

protocols.title: Information-flow structure
protocols.finding: q information flows from state to prepared key to cache; residual content flows through an avoidable inputBits copy before dense own cofactor; exact values flow backward across task/q dependencies. Dense load-transform fusion is candidate.

protocols.title: Causal / temporal structure
protocols.finding: First-win stopping is a causal cut: once mover transition terminalizes, no later future-game state exists. Current q lookup occurs after terminalization at recursive entry and opponent cofactor is computed before terminal recognition. Stage A terminal-before-q is candidate; Stage B post-win blocker suppression requires explicit terminal-state scope.

protocols.title: Containment / ownership structure
protocols.finding: Generic q cache owns arbitrary payload semantics and Branch Manager object-valued q nodes; ordinary worker owns WDL-only values. This ownership boundary blocks global Int8 conversion and permits only scoped specialization.

protocols.title: Cardinality / multiplicity structure
protocols.finding: Ordinary WDL has cardinality three while generic cache value domain is open; pair-incidence records have repeated word multiplicity; one canonical q can have many parent/task occurrences. These counts are optimization cues, not identity evidence.

protocols.title: Dual / reversed structures
protocols.finding: Own and blocker cofactors are complementary player-event roles but not interchangeable algorithms; global own normalization prevents mechanically importing block locality. Existing dense-own/block separation is retained.

protocols.title: Complement / exclusion structure
protocols.finding: First-win stopping excludes post-terminal continuation semantics; sealed storage excludes growth; unresolved proof guards exclude optimistic applicability. Terminal boundary candidate uses only the first exclusion.

protocols.title: Fixed-point / recurrence structure
protocols.finding: Ordinary game value is rank-well-founded, not intrinsically a global fixed point. Current task quantum is execution policy over that DAG. Existing rank-cut/supply-front candidates remain valid; terminal nodes are recurrence leaves and need not be nonterminal q cache entries.

protocols.title: Compositional-structure discovery
protocols.finding: ownTransition composes class load then dense transform then normalization; the first two can potentially fuse without changing composition semantics. q mirror canonicalization similarly composes orbit selection with exact triple representation.

protocols.title: Reconstruction-structure discovery
protocols.finding: supportLo/supportHi are reconstructible from gravity support/heights and are consumed by optional proof guards, while ordinary workers exclude certificates/RBA. A worker-only omission could be possible, but specialization/branching economics and public-state reconstruction obligations are unresolved; no issue filed.

protocols.title: Proof / witness topology
protocols.finding: 0.1 native NEI records lacked proper A/B/P/E claim topology. Corrected NEI 0.2 uses ^94000/01/02/03/07/08/10/11/17/24/25 roles. q/proof identity remains separate.

protocols.title: Refinement-relation discovery
protocols.finding: NEI application 0.2 corrects an invalid identity-strengthening in 0.1; it is a corrective successor/revision of that qualification layer, not evidence-narrowing refinement. Runtime observations from 0.1 remain valid.

protocols.title: Boundary-movement invariance
protocols.finding: Moving growU32 to module scope changed runtime allocation without semantic change, proving administrative/source boundary can matter to machine realization. Support-first q candidate moves the mirror-decision boundary while preserving the q orbit; must not move proof-transporter authority.

protocols.title: Parameter-role correspondence
protocols.finding: worker count, node quantum, 512 poll interval, 64K transition prefix and retention caps have distinct resource/control roles. Existing #75/#79/#94 evidence already owns them; numerical coincidence gives no new relation.

protocols.title: Dimensional / unit structure
protocols.finding: Fixed widths (42 cells, 20 frontier words, 10 chunks, 32-bit words, 3 WDL values) explain several exact specializations, but width alone does not authorize a representation change. New fixed-width cache candidate is ownership-scoped in #101.

protocols.title: Ordering / partial-order structure
protocols.finding: Support-local action-value isotony and task dependency leverage remain separate ordering relations. Move-order pair record term IDs are monotone enough to make same-word reuse possible without reordering advisory semantics.

protocols.title: Reachability / connectivity structure
protocols.finding: Manager q graph exposes only part of worker-internal reachability; rank-cut #89 targets earlier convergence. Terminal states are absorbing leaves, reinforcing #98. No hidden bypass invalidates first-win stopping.

protocols.title: Conservation / balance structure
protocols.finding: Exact apply/undo, prepared-key bit preservation, mirror orbit equality and WDL invariance are conservation obligations across optimized representations. They are qualification constraints, not new semantics.

protocols.title: Threshold / phase-boundary structure
protocols.finding: Measured thresholds 64K transition prefix, 512 necessity poll, worker-count-dependent quantum, and retention caps are policy boundaries. Empty-root class high-water crosses the four-worker retention share, but #84 already found existing hysteresis effective and lacks a new measured case; retain as QU observation only.

protocols.title: Degenerate / special-case structure
protocols.finding: Terminal states, horizontally symmetric supports, singleton terms, empty residuals and forced edges expose simpler exact structures. Terminal special case -> #98; support stabilizer is the only case where #97 still needs residual tie-break.

protocols.title: Failure-mode correspondence
protocols.finding: Rejected hit-first interning, blocker memo, trusted fast paths and manager epochs share a failure mode: source-operation reduction/reuse did not improve end-to-end economics. This is a negative discovery law used to gate new candidates.

protocols.title: Exception-structure discovery
protocols.finding: Exceptions define lawful optimization scopes: support symmetry for residual mirror tie-break; terminal states for q bypass; proof-enabled states for support masks; object-valued manager cache for generic payload. Exceptions prevent over-generalizing candidates.

protocols.title: Representation-redundancy discovery
protocols.finding: Confirmed past redundancies: general Number carriers, runtime cell masks, object pair incidence, singleton scan, lexical helper context. New candidates: support-first avoids unnecessary residual reflection, WDL specialization avoids general payload only at ordinary-worker boundary, dense own copy may be redundant. supportLo/Hi redundancy remains open.

protocols.title: Equivalent constraint-closure discovery
protocols.finding: Operation-word signed/unsigned forms can be equivalent under exact projected consumer closure, but equivalence does not automatically imply NEI SAME. Corrected profile supplies explicit identity law only for NEI-HOT-001/002. Mirror canonical representative alternatives preserve the same exact reflection equivalence class.

protocols.title: Semantic-identity candidate discovery
protocols.finding: Full NEI audit found 0.1 overreach. Corrected 0.2 qualifies only two determinate operation-word SAME claims; hash-vs-q has no NEI claim; task-occurrence/q is contextual only; standard-7x6 q NEI remains INCOMPLETE_UNQUALIFIED; #96 remains unqualified.

protocols.title: QUI extension from partial unknown correspondence
protocols.finding: QU-HOT-01/02/03 are different unknown questions with no qualified structural isomorphism target. Equal uncertainty shape would not establish identity or optimization equivalence. No QUI is proposed.

protocols.title: Global whole-structure isomorphism
protocols.finding: Semantic, source, V8, machine and scheduling layers are intentionally not globally isomorphic. The useful object is a typed causal correspondence with residuals/unknowns. Whole-graph isomorphism would erase load-bearing implementation distinctions.

protocols.title: Literal-value coincidence
protocols.finding: Repeated values such as 32, 42, 64K or 512 are meaningful only with their structural roles. No candidate is based on literal coincidence.

protocols.title: Lexical / name similarity
protocols.finding: Labels such as hot/cold, cache, frontier or identity are retrieval hints only. The cold-helper result is a direct counterexample to trusting lexical hot/cold classification as machine behavior.

protocols.title: Shared ontology / class-label hints
protocols.finding: Shared class/module labels did not supply optimization authority. Generic cache and ordinary WDL cache share ontology labels but differ in ownership; structural contract wins.

protocols.title: Serialization / layout similarity
protocols.finding: Flat numeric layout was historically beneficial, but layout similarity alone is not evidence. Native .isg/JSON/JS layout differences carry no identity claim; runtime layout changes require exact A/B qualification.

protocols.title: Raw identifier correspondence
protocols.finding: Pool-local residual class IDs, task IDs, SIs and hash values are addressing only. They are not portable q/NEI/proof identity. This explicitly blocks shared-TT schemes keyed directly by worker class IDs.
